content: We communicate with the user in German; all persisted writing (code, comments, commit messages, issues, documentation) stays in English.

After changing function signatures in the dagmar Dagger module (.dagger/main.go), run dagger develop to regenerate the on-disk client (dagger.gen.go, internal/dagger/*.gen.go). dagger call and dagger functions regenerate internally at RUNTIME, so execution keeps working, but the on-disk generated code and thus gopls/IDE stay stale and report undefined errors on removed functions until dagger develop runs.

dagmar Dagger module layout: dagger.json at the repo root with source=.dagger, code under .dagger/. dagger init --source=.dagger creates .dagger/{main.go, internal/dagger, dagger.gen.go, go.mod, go.sum}. The .dagger dir has its OWN go.mod (module dagger/dagmar) because Go ignores dot-directories in a normal module build, so the Dagger module must be self-contained and isolated from the root github.com/denkhaus/dagmar go.mod (which lives in the shared go.work). The root Go build never sees .dagger/ by design.

Do NOT delete the .dagger generated files (.dagger/dagger.gen.go, .dagger/internal/dagger/). They are git-ignored (not committed) but REQUIRED locally: .dagger/main.go imports the generated client package dagger/dagmar/internal/dagger (uses dagger.K3SOpts, *dagger.K3S, etc.), so deleting them breaks compilation (gopls/IDE shows errors in main.go). They regenerate on every dagger develop/call. On a fresh clone, run dagger develop once to generate them. (Ignoring them is the Dagger convention; committing them is an option but causes git churn on regen.)
